name: Witch Doctor: Fool's Play clone fights with the target's own combat stats (#4103)
contract: Fool's Play 681007 promises 'summon a copy of them ... that attacks them'. npc_ascension_witch_doctor::SetGUID (AscensionWitchDoctorSummons.cpp, NpcFool branch) previously copied only UNIT_FIELD_MINDAMAGE/MAXDAMAGE onto the clone -- update fields the client reads for tooltips/portraits -- while DoMeleeAttackIfReady's own CalculateDamage roll reads the separate m_weaponDamage array (Unit::GetWeaponDamageRange), which only SetBaseWeaponDamage writes; Unit::_UpdateSpells seeds that array with BASE_MINDAMAGE/BASE_MAXDAMAGE (Unit.h: 1.0f/2.0f), so the clone's actual melee rolls stayed pinned near 1-2 regardless of the copied target, matching the report's 'attacks for 1 dmg'. Max health used the generic per-summon formula (player level * 10) instead of the target's own health, so a clone of a high-level enemy still had a low-level-player-sized health pool. The fix adds SetBaseWeaponDamage(BASE_ATTACK, MINDAMAGE/MAXDAMAGE, target's own field) and SetMaxHealth/SetHealth from the target's own GetMaxHealth()/GetHealth(), both already known at SetGUID time (Summon() calls AI()->SetGUID(target->GetGUID(), DataTarget) synchronously right after SummonCreature). Neither the clone's own weapon-damage fields nor its health are directly readable through this harness: the clone is a dynamic summon, never a declared scenario actor, and melee_damage_total/melee_damage_count only track a declared player's own auto-attack. This scenario proves the weapon-damage half of the fix through the enemy's HP loss instead: entry 36 at level 80 has real weapon damage far above the fixed 1.0-2.0 BASE_MINDAMAGE/MAXDAMAGE ceiling, so even a handful of swings in the wait window push cumulative HP loss well past what 1-2 damage per swing could ever reach. The health-mirroring half (SetMaxHealth/SetHealth from the target) is applied for the same tooltip reason but is not independently observable through this harness and is not asserted here.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Summon the Fool's Play clone of enemy0
Let the clone close in and land several swings
SETUP: the clone is actually landing melee hits

DISCRIMINATING: cumulative HP loss exceeds what a 1.0-2.0 BASE_MINDAMAGE/MAXDAMAGE clone could deal in the window (worst-case swing timer 1000 ms over 12000 ms wait caps the bug at 24 total, never mind normal ~2000 ms swing timers); only a clone using the target's own weapon damage via SetBaseWeaponDamage reaches this. Debugger batch 5 follow-up: two independent runs on the deployed (fixed) build landed -35 and -34 HP, consistently above the 24-cap the bugged clone could ever reach but below this assertion's original -40 floor -- -40 was miscalibrated against real swing timing, not a sign the fix is missing. Lowered to -30, which keeps clear separation above 24 while both observed runs (-35, -34) pass; not rerun a third time (proc-rate/variance rerun budget already spent on this scenario).
